subject: Notice: addition of EdgeNimbus as processing partner - evidence requested
messages:
From: Alan Chang <alan.chang@lucentcloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: maya.patel@lucentcloud.com
Date: 2026-08-12T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Notice: addition of EdgeNimbus as processing partner

Hi Kimberly & Karthik,

As discussed on our call last week, LucentCloud is adding EdgeNimbus LLC as a processing partner for edge telemetry routing in the EU and US regions. EdgeNimbus will provide transient caching and telemetry aggregation for a subset of our LucentCloud customers; they will handle pseudonymized logs and aggregated metrics only.

Per our DPA, we wanted to notify Redwood Inference and provide the initial manifest and attestations. Attached: edge-nimbus-manifest.csv (processor list + country footprint). We also have a short SOC2 excerpt which I'll send in the follow-up.

Could you confirm the DPA addendum review path on your side and let us know if you need onshore fallback guarantees for any EU workloads? We're prepared to provide a DocuSign addendum if that speeds review.

Thanks,

Alan Chang
Head of Integrations, LucentCloud
alan.chang@lucentcloud.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachments: edge-nimbus-manifest.csv (csv, 8KB)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Alan Chang <alan.chang@lucentcloud.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-12T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of EdgeNimbus as processing partner

Alan — thanks for the heads-up and the manifest. Quick checklist from our side to keep the review moving: 

- Full processor manifest (you attached the CSV; please confirm it includes sub-tier subprocessors and regions).
- SOC2 summary or equivalent controls snapshot (test coverage for ingestion and access controls).
- Data flow diagram for the telemetry path (what leaves LucentCloud vs. stays on EdgeNimbus).
- Encryption at-rest/transit and KMS details (who holds keys for logs if any).
- Retention and deletion commitments (how long aggregated telemetry is kept).

Could you attach the SOC2 excerpt and a redlined DPA addendum (if you have one) to the Google Drive link you shared? We'll run this through our intake: Rishi (cc'd) will do the controls/technical review, Karthik will handle the legal/DPA redline. I can route approvals once we have the artifacts — expected internal SLA is 7 business days for a standard partner addition, faster if we get SOC2 and KMS attestations.

Also, flagging an immediate question: do any EdgeNimbus nodes process raw customer request payloads or only aggregated metrics? If raw payloads are in scope we need a different escalation.

Thanks — Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Privacy & Compliance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

---
Attachment stubs referenced: edge-nimbus-manifest.csv (received)

From: Alan Chang <alan.chang@lucentcloud.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@lucentcloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of EdgeNimbus as processing partner

Kimberly — thanks for the quick checklist. Short answers inline: 

- The CSV includes sub-tier entries in a separate tab; I'll upload the flattened export to the Drive folder now.
- SOC2: attached as edge-nimbus-soc2-summary.pdf (redacted; includes control mapping for ingestion, encryption, and change management).
- Data flow: EdgeNimbus processes only aggregated telemetry and anonymized metrics. No raw request payloads are sent.
- Keys: EdgeNimbus uses LucentCloud-managed KMS keys; no customer-managed keys are shared. Encryption in transit is TLS1.3.
- Retention: default retention 30 days for aggregated telemetry, configurable to 7 days on request.

I've uploaded the SOC2 excerpt and a proposed DPA addendum (lucentcloud-dpa-addendum.docx) to the Drive link and also prepared a DocuSign envelope for Redwood's signature to formalize the addendum: https://docusign.example.com/Envelope/12345abcdef.

Let us know if the 30-day retention and LucentCloud KMS approach are blockers; if so we can discuss onshore escrow/fallback options for specific customers.

Best,
Alan

Attachments: edge-nimbus-soc2-summary.pdf (pdf, 120KB); lucentcloud-dpa-addendum.docx (docx, 35KB)

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.com <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Alan Chang <alan.chang@lucentcloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-12T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Notice: addition of EdgeNimbus as processing partner

Thanks Alan — reviewed the artifacts at a high level. Two legal notes and next steps: 

1) The proposed DPA addendum is mostly standard; I'll prepare a redline focused on the following items: data subject scope (explicitly call out telemetry and aggregated metrics), liability cap carveouts for telemetry retention, and audit rights for onshore customers. Expect the redline this afternoon.

2) For onshore fallback: if specific customers require data to remain within a jurisdiction, LucentCloud should indicate if EdgeNimbus can be restricted by region or an onshore proxy can be used. Rishi, please advise technical feasibility on the KMS/retention front and whether 30-day retention is acceptable for most customers.

Kimberly — once the redline is ready, please route to Procurement for countersignature and to the CS lead on the customer side for any contract-specific carveouts. Alan — we'll attempt to turn this within 5 business days if no significant issues show up on the controls review.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Commercial | Redwood Inference
